paragraphs.text: 1. Deccan Rabi Food-Grain Basin (Southern Maharashtra & Northern Karnataka)
Strategic Role: The culinary, grading, and marketing center of high-value edible white sorghum.
Solapur & Barshi APMCs (Maharashtra): The largest commercial trading yards for Maldandi grain in India; equipped with high-speed pneumatic cleaners, destoners, and flour-milling units.
Vijayapura & Bagalkote Mandis (Karnataka): Central aggregation point for Bili Jola.

Infrastructure Profile: Mechanized de-hulling plants, grain polishers, and stover densification/baling plants that compress bulky dry sorghum stalks (kadbi) into high-density blocks for transport to drought-hit dairy tracts.
Catchment Areas: Solapur, Ahilyanagar, Dharashiv, Beed, Sangli (Maharashtra); Vijayapura, Bagalkote, Kalaburagi, Belagavi (Karnataka).

paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: The national research, processing incubation, and corporate value-addition engine for millets.

Key Facilities: Headquarters of the ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (IIMR) at Rajendranagar, housing the Nutrihub Incubation Centre; pilot processing lines for puffing, flaking, cold-extrusion, and bakery blending; major modern grain distilleries operating in Medak and Nalgonda.
Catchment Areas: Semi-arid plateau production from Mahabubnagar, Sangareddy, Vikarabad (Telangana); inflows of irrigated zero-till grain from Guntur and Palnadu (Andhra Pradesh).

protection.name: Sorghum Shoot Fly (Atherigona soccata)
protection.geography: National Epidemic Threat (Severe in late-sown Kharif & Rabi)
protection.impact: Small whitish maggot crawls down the leaf sheath and cuts the growing point of 7-to-25-day-old seedlings; central leaf turns yellow, wilts, and dries up, forming a foul-smelling "Dead Heart" that pulls out easily; damaged plants produce weak, unproductive tillers.
protection.passage: Jowar — source table 99, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Grain Mold Complex (Fusarium moniliforme, Curvularia lunata, Alternaria spp.)
protection.geography: All Kharif Rainfed Belts (Devastating during wet Sept–Oct harvests)
protection.impact: Grains develop velvety pink, white, or black fungal crusts during development and maturity; endosperm disintegrates into chalky powder; seed germination drops; produces toxic mycotoxins (zearalenone, fumonisins), rendering grain unmarketable for human food.
protection.passage: Jowar — source table 99, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Spotted Stem Borer (Chilo partellus)
protection.impact: Young larvae feed inside the leaf whorl, causing parallel rows of circular pinholes ("shot holes"); older larvae bore into the central stem, tunneling through the pith; causes dead hearts in older plants, broken peduncles, and stunted, chaffy earheads.
protection.passage: Jowar — source table 99, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Charcoal Rot / Stalk Rot (Macrophomina phaseolina)
protection.impact: Post-flowering lodging; lower stem internodes become soft, discolored, and spongy; internal pith disintegrates, leaving separated vascular bundles covered in thousands of tiny, jet-black charcoal-like sclerotial bodies; stems snap at ground level during late-season terminal drought.
protection.passage: Jowar — source table 99, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Fall Armyworm (FAW) (Spodoptera frugiperda)
protection.impact: Caterpillars shelter deep inside the whorl, chewing broad ragged holes and depositing large piles of moist sawdust-like fecal frass; can defoliate entire seedling canopies within days.
protection.passage: Jowar — source table 99, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rice Weevil & Grain Moth (Sitophilus oryzae, Sitotroga cerealella)
protection.geography: All Mandi Depots & Stored Grain Warehouses
protection.impact: Adult weevils and larvae bore into stored whole sorghum grains; excavate hollow cavities, leaving fine flour dust; grain moth larvae spin silky webs across the surface of grain heaps; reduces grain weight and seed viability.
protection.passage: Jowar — source table 99, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
